# Introduction

Hello and welcome!

I'm James Christopher (Chris) Slaughter, an Associate Professor in the Department of Biostatistics at Vanderbilt University Medical Center.  This is my professional web page, which is currently under development.


# Research Interests

My research interests include:

- Longitudinal Data Analysis for Observational Studies
- Latent Variable Methods
- Bayesian Statistics
- Pediatrics, Gastroenterology, and Reproductive Health applications

# Short Bio

I am an Associate Professor of Biostatistics at Vanderbilt University Medical Center. I received my M.S. in Biostatistics from the University of Washington and my Dr.P.H. in Biostatistics from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, where my doctoral research focused on Bayesian latent variable models for longitudinal processes.

My work centers on collaborative research across a wide range of clinical areas, including pediatrics, gastroenterology, and infectious disease. I partner with investigators on the design and analysis of clinical trials and observational studies, with particular interests in longitudinal data and Bayesian modeling. In addition to my collaborative work, I also teach graduate courses in regression methods and survival analysis and mentor trainees from biostatistics, epidemiology, and clinical disciplines
